newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Hubco at odds with utility over credit.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Hubco at odds with utility over credit.

text.p: Pakistan's private Hub Power Co (Hubco) said on Thursday the state power utility had failed to supply a letter of credit required under the terms of a power purchase agreement.

"The company is reviewing its options, including, but not limited to, asking for assistance from the government of Pakistan, to resolve this matter," Hubco said in a notice to investors at the Karachi Stock Exchange.

It said the power purchase contract with the state-run Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) required it to issue a replacement letter of credit not later than 30 days before the expiry of an earlier one.
The letter of credit covers WAPDA's projected payments to Hubco for two months' supply of electricity, as a guarantee against default. The current one expires on June 30, Hubco said.
"WAPDA in compliance with its obligations under the power purchase agreement should, therefore, have provided the company with a replacement letter of credit no later than May 31, 1997.
"As at this date, WAPDA has not provided the company with a replacement letter of credit," the notice said.
No WAPDA official was immediately available for comment.

A Hubco spokesman said: "WAPDA has not stopped payments for the power it is purchasing, but the letter of credit is needed under the agreement as a security which the company can encash in case WAPDA fails to stay with its payment schedule."
Last month, WAPDA threatened to scrap its power purchase agreement with Hubco on the grounds that electricity meters at the plant near Karachi had been tampered with.
Hubco denied the allegation and the government intervened to resolve the matter.
Britain's National Power and Saudi Arabia's Xenel Industries Ltd have major stakes in the World Bank-backed, $1.5-billion 1,292-megawatt Hubco plant completed in February.
Hubco's 10-rupee stock tumbled to a low of 40.40 rupees from a high of 41.30 on Thursday after the notice was announced on the floor of the Karachi Stock Exchange.
But the blue-chip scrip soon bounced back and by 0748 GMT it was 0.85 rupees up at 41.20 rupees from its previous close.

"The stock is still in demand on foreign buying, but as the news spreads, and if the matter is not resolved, investors may square out of Hubco," dealer Zaina Nowsherwan of BMA Capital Management said. ($1 = 40.49 rupees)
